picks.headline: Meta releases Low Precision FlashAttention-4 with MXFP8 support for Blackwell GPUs
picks.why: It achieves up to 2.85 PF/s on Nvidia Blackwell hardware by using MXFP8 block-scaled attention for both forward and backward passes.
picks.title: Low Precision Flash Attention 4: End-to-End Block-Scaled Attention for Blackwell

picks.headline: OpenAI introduces standardized reporting framework for model misalignment incidents
picks.why: OpenAI is formalizing how safety anomalies and unexpected model behaviors are tracked and disclosed, releasing six initial incident reports alongside the framework.
picks.title: Our framework for reporting model misalignment

picks.headline: Cross-channel payload fragmentation attacks bypass Model Context Protocol security defenses
picks.why: Attackers can split malicious payloads across separate MCP context channels to achieve complete credential exfiltration against agentic workflows.
picks.title: Measuring and Exploiting Implicit Trust in LLM Tool-Calling Pipelines

picks.headline: NVIDIA debuts Vera Rubin NVL72 showing 3.7x throughput jump in MLPerf
picks.why: The preview benchmarks demonstrate significant generational performance improvements over GB300 systems on complex reasoning and vision-language models.
picks.title: NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 Delivers Leading Performance in MLPerf Inference v6.1 Debut

picks.headline: Poisoned evaluation benchmarks exploit self-modifying AI coding agents in compiler attack
picks.why: This attack adapts the classic 'Trusting Trust' vector to autonomous coders by corrupting their self-evaluation suites during optimization loops.
picks.title: Reflections on Trusting Trust, Revisited: Contaminating Self-Modifying AI Coding Agents with Poisoned Benchmarks

picks.headline: Model Context Protocol agent traffic evades detection by standard network NIDS
picks.why: MCP agent traffic structurally mimics command-and-control beaconing while bypassing current network intrusion detection signatures and behavioral scoring.
picks.title: When Agents Look Like Beacons: NIDS Evasion by Model Context Protocol Traffic

picks.headline: NVIDIA introduces cuTile Rust for writing tile-based CUDA kernels in Rust
picks.why: It enables authoring high-performance GPU tile operations directly in Rust to bring memory safety and better ergonomics to low-level kernel development.
picks.title: Translating CUDA Tile Operations from Python to Rust Using Agentic AI

picks.headline: Internal state difference vectors detect LLM reward hacking at zero compute cost
picks.why: Linear difference-of-means vectors derived from internal activations can reliably flag and predict reward-hacking behaviors during model evaluations.
picks.title: Monitoring and Discovering Reward Hacking with Internal Representations during LLM Evaluations

papers.headline: Onset Refusal Collapse reveals first-token safety failure in large reasoning models
papers.why: It identifies that reasoning models frequently suffer safety failures due to a localized breakdown at the very first generated token.
papers.title: First Token Matters: Understanding Safety Collapse in Large Reasoning Models

papers.headline: Hypernetworks enable infinite-parameter LLMs with real-time dynamic weight generation
papers.why: This architecture replaces static feed-forward layers with a hypernetwork that generates dynamic low-rank weight updates directly from live user interactions.
papers.title: Infinite-Parameter LLMs: Generating and Adapting Weights from Live Data

papers.headline: HOPE framework applies second-order optimization to prune MoE model experts
papers.why: It accounts for cooperative expert interactions during compression, enabling significantly higher MoE pruning rates without sacrificing downstream performance.
papers.title: Higher-order pruning of experts in mixture-of-experts language models
